task.goal: Send a support request and know it was received
task.starting_conditions: A signed-out visitor has their name, email and a description; the local demonstration service can accept, reject or delay a request
task.expected_outcome: One request is accepted and confirmation is visible; input mistakes and temporary failures can be corrected without re-entering valid work
task.device_input: Desktop keyboard and pointer, plus a 375px-wide mobile viewport
task.source: User's requested UX review demonstration, especially validation recovery and preservation of completed form entries
assumptions: This is an isolated demonstration, not a real support service
Name, email and request are required
The local service is simulated; no messages or personal information leave the browser
Cancel during saving preserves the draft and prevents a later success message
acceptance: The primary action describes sending a request
Missing or invalid information is identified with a useful correction
A rejected email preserves the entered name and request
Keyboard users can discover the error and correct it
Correcting only the email permits completion without re-entering other fields
While saving, progress is visible and repeat submission is prevented
Cancellation and temporary failure preserve entries and permit retry
The form remains usable at 375px without horizontal scrolling
